# OpenAI Staffer Likely Captured Secrets on Hidden Bug, US Says

![The Phillip Burton Federal Building and US Courthouse during a detention hearing for Abdulrahman Alfozan in San Francisco, on Oct. 19.](https://assets.bwbx.io/images/users/iqjWHBFdfxIU/iIlidl_5HwTk/v1/-1x-1.webp)

The Phillip Burton Federal Building and US Courthouse during a detention hearing for Abdulrahman Alfozan in San Francisco, on Oct. 19. Photographer: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg

By Madlin Mekelburg

November 23, 2026 at 11:56 PM UTC

US prosecutors say the former engineer at OpenAI charged with bugging an office conference room likely intercepted trade secrets and possessed a photograph of what appears to be a term sheet for a “strategic partnership” between the ChatGPT maker and another company.

In a Monday court filing, prosecutors urged a federal judge to deny the latest request by Abdulrahman Alfozan to be released on bail while the criminal case against him proceeds. They said their investigation into Alfozan is ongoing, but they remain concerned he might try to flee before trial given his relatively weak ties to the US and the considerable resources and connections he has in his native Saudi Arabia.
